Models with reconciled forecasts

Source: R/hierarchy.R
reconciled.Rd

Wraps a model specification so that its forecasts are reconciled over a hierarchy every time it is forecast, also inside mt_backtest(). If the training data contain only the bottom strata, the aggregate strata are added with mt_aggregate_strata() before fitting, so that the base model forecasts every node. Predictive draws (used by backtests) are coherent as well: Poisson and extra-Poisson variation are drawn for the bottom strata only and the aggregates are their sums.

Usage

reconciled(
  spec,
  hierarchy,
  method = c("wls", "mint", "structural", "ols", "bottom_up", "proportional"),
  shrink = "auto",
  dependence = c("auto", "empirical", "none"),
  fixed = NULL
)

Arguments

spec

Base model specification (fitted to all strata).

hierarchy

An mt_hierarchy().

method, shrink

See mt_reconcile().

dependence

"auto" (default: "none" for models fitted jointly across strata, whose draws already carry their dependence, such as li_lee() and tucker3(); "empirical" for models fitted per stratum), "empirical" or "none". With "empirical" the same training years order the paths before reconciliation and the predictive noise of the bottom strata, so aggregates of predictive draws keep the observed co-movement.

fixed

Strata whose forecasts are kept (see mt_reconcile()).

Value

A model specification.

Details

On mt_example_regions() (4 regions, 90 strata, origins 2005 and 2008, h = 10), li_lee(common_by = "sex") with method = "bottom_up" was the most accurate coherent forecast (CRPS 0.0425 bottom, 0.0269 aggregates; 95% coverage 0.95), and Lee-Carter per stratum with "wls" reconciliation was calibrated (0.95-0.97) but less accurate (0.0477, 0.0292). On the ONS and German regional data, reconciliation changed the accuracy of the bottom strata little and lowered the coverage of the totals (see the vignette "Coherent forecasts: what reconciliation changes").

Examples

x <- mt_example_regions(years = 2000:2019, regions = 3)
h <- mt_hierarchy(sex = "both", region = "all", quintile = "all")
fit <- mt_fit(reconciled(lee_carter(), h, method = "wls"), mt_aggregate_strata(x, h))
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 5, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
